chief_complaint: Request acceptance at a higher-level center and close the transport loop

team_brief.title: Transfer request: septic shock
team_brief.location: Small hospital without ICU or overnight urology
team_brief.situation: Septic shock from an obstructed infected kidney; she needs ICU support and urologic source control.
background: CT shows an 8 mm obstructing ureteric stone with hydronephrosis.
current_status: Norepinephrine 0.08 mcg/kg/min through a peripheral line after 2 L crystalloid.
BP 92/58, lactate improved from 5.0 to 3.8, SpO2 95% on 2 L nasal cannula.
key_data: Ongoing vasopressor requirement and obstructed infection require higher-level care.
treatments: Confirm whether urology has been informed and how transport will be monitored.
team_brief.your_request: Request acceptance, destination, monitored transport plan, and clear responsibility during transfer.
must_include: Current vasopressor support, response, and source-control need.
Acceptance, bed destination, transport monitoring, and escalation contact.

kickoff_text: This is Dr. Bennett at the regional ICU. Tell me why your patient needs transfer.
persona_override: You are Dr. Bennett, an ICU attending at a regional referral center. The caller works at a small hospital without an ICU. The patient is Ms. Laura King, 61, with obstructed infected kidney and septic shock. She is on norepinephrine through a peripheral line at 0.08 mcg/kg/min after 2 L crystalloid; BP is 92/58, lactate fell from 5.0 to 3.8, oxygen saturation is 95% on 2 L nasal cannula. Piperacillin-tazobactam was given; CT shows an 8 mm obstructing ureteric stone with hydronephrosis. Ask why local care is insufficient, whether urology knows, and how transport will be monitored. Accept the transfer once the learner gives a structured handover and explicitly requests acceptance. Confirm bed destination and responsibility during transport.
learning_objectives: state the urgent transfer request and reason for higher-level care
summarize hemodynamic status, treatment, response, and source control need
explain the referring hospital's capability limitation
confirm acceptance, destination, transport monitoring, and interim responsibility
suggested_questions: I'm requesting urgent transfer for ICU support and urologic source control.
We do not have an ICU or overnight urology service at this hospital.
Can you confirm acceptance, the receiving unit, and who I should update if she deteriorates in transit?

clinical_knowledge.topic: Interfacility transfer request for septic shock requiring ICU and urologic source control
core_concepts: A transfer call must explain both the patient's clinical need and the referring site's capability gap.
Transfer of responsibility is incomplete until acceptance, destination, transport, monitoring, and interim ownership are confirmed.
diagnostic_clues: An obstructed infected collecting system creates a time-sensitive source-control need.
common_misconceptions: A clinical summary alone constitutes a transfer request.
Acceptance automatically defines transport responsibility and the receiving location.
dangerous_errors: Omitting vasopressor support, response to treatment, or source-control need.
Moving the patient without explicit acceptance and a monitored transport plan.
management_principles: Continue time-critical sepsis treatment and reassessment while arranging higher-level care.
Use a structured handoff and closed loop at every transition of accountability.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Transfer eligibility, stabilization, transport staffing, legal obligations, and source-control timing depend on local and regional systems.
